contentBlocks.text: All week you've built one piece at a time: thesis, two body paragraphs, transitions, and a conclusion. Today, assemble the complete, finished essay.

Quick review: a strong essay has a specific thesis (Day 1), body paragraphs built from Claim-Evidence-Reasoning (Day 2), essay-level transitions connecting paragraphs (Day 3), and a synthesizing conclusion that answers 'so what?' (Day 4). Gather everything you wrote this week and combine it into one complete 4-paragraph essay: introduction with your thesis, two body paragraphs with their transition, and your conclusion. Read the whole essay aloud, checking it flows as one connected argument.
You just wrote a complete, genuinely sophisticated 4-paragraph formal essay. This is real academic writing, and this same structure will support every essay you write from here forward.

objectives: Recall all components of a formal essay: thesis, body paragraphs, transitions, conclusion
Assemble the week's separate pieces into one complete, coherent 4-paragraph essay
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child assemble their complete essay using this week's pieces.
3. Read the finished essay aloud together, checking it reads as one connected argument, not four separate pieces.
4. Celebrate finishing a real, complete formal essay — a genuine step up from Grade 5's persuasive paragraph.
5. Note this same 4-part structure (thesis/body/transitions/conclusion) will apply to every future essay this year.
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow light editing help (spelling, minor wording) as long as the 4-part structure is the child's own work
Ready for more: ask them to add a third body paragraph with its own transition, extending the essay further
This is a genuine finished-writing milestone — more sophisticated than Grade 5's simpler opinion paragraph, worth explicitly celebrating as a step up
teacherGuide.answerKey: Answers will vary — check the finished essay includes a specific thesis, two body paragraphs each with claim/evidence/reasoning, a transition connecting them, and a synthesizing conclusion — reading as one coherent essay, not four disconnected pieces.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Synthesizes the full week's Common Core Grade 8 Writing standards (W.8.1a-e) into one complete formal essay, matching the course's own 'formal essay writing' description end to end.
